newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall Street rebound sparks Euroshare rally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall Street rebound sparks Euroshare rally.

text.p: European shares had extended an early rally by midday on Friday, reflecting switchback trading overnight on Wall Street, which tumbled and then rebounded as New Year bargain hunters came out in force.
Europe's three key bourses, London, Frankfurt and Paris, were up some 0.6, 1.2 and 0.7 percent, respectively, after falling much more heavily on Thursday.

Wall Street's Dow Jones industrial average began some 20 points firmer on Thursday, only to plunge 96 points into the minus column, before clawing its way back to finish the day down just 5.78 points at 6,442.49.
On Tuesday, before the New Year holiday, it shed 101 points.

U.S. analysts said the heavy early selling appeared to be an over-reaction to a report of robust manufacturing activity in December in part because so many traders and investors were still enjoying New Year vacations.

"A lot of people that weren't working decided to call in late and say, "Start buying these things'," Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital, said of Wall Street's performance.
U.S. shares are prey to fears that too rapid growth in the world's number one economy might lead to higher interest rates, which would undermine soaring share valuations.
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 25.7 points at 4,083.1 after stumbling 61.1 points, or about 1.5 percent, on Thursday.
"If the Dow opens 20 or 30 points higher, we could end up 30 to 40 points better on the day," one broker said.
Yet with trading volumes still so low, it was too early to predict the market's direction, one London dealer said.

"I've spoken to only a few clients so far today," said another trader. "Volume is thin and with U.S. markets so volatile in the last few days, there doesn't seem to be anyone around who wants to make a bet."

French stocks rallied in line with other European bourses and also got a small boost from the government's nomination to the Bank of France monetary policy council of two candidates viewed as favourable to easier interest rates, brokers said.
The government nominated Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard, replacing two outgoing members -- including Jean Boissonnat -- viewed as being from the strong franc camp.

"The nominations helped a bit because the two are apparently favourable to rate cuts but the reaction is very limited," a trader said. "The market is mainly focused on what's going on in the United States."
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 16.29 points at 2,273.26 after easing from a session high of 2,271.31 right after the nominations were announced.
Germany's electronically traded Ibis DAX index rose sharply in pre-bourse trading, having fallen heavily in Thursday's post-bourse session. It was up 32.99 points at 2,853.80 points.
The DAX index of floor trading was up just 3.88 points, however, having closed before Wall's Street's latest gyrations.
In currencies, the dollar rallied to 1.550 marks and 115.77 yen in early Europe after tracking asset markets lower on Thursday following the strong U.S. economic data.
"People are generally quite bullish on the dollar," said a corporate dealer at German bank. Traders also said the dollar's recovery on Friday was led by a climb in sterling.
Profit-taking, after a climb to four-year highs, knocked sterling to lows of 2.5942 marks in overnight Europe on Thursday and $1.6828 lows against the dollar.
"A lot of the selling of dollars was due to the selloff in sterling," said Bank of Boston FX dealer Peter Wood.
But sterling's recovery on Friday was emulated by dollar strength. At midday sterling was at $1.6953.
The market is now awaiting U.S. November construction spending at 1500 gmt for fresh direction.

Gold, sometimes seen as a hedge against inflation, fell further in early European trading, with traders puzzled by its weakness in the face of concern that inflation might re-emerge. It fixed at $364.30, its lowest since November 3, 1993.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.5500 marks and 115.77 yen, compared with 1.5407 and 115.47 in late trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares rose 25.7 points to 4,083.1.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 3.88 at 2,852.65.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index rose 16.29 to 2,273.26.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $364.30, compared with London's close on Thursday of $366.85. Silver eased two cents to $4.71.
